[Erowid Note: 
Cannabis substitute "spice" type smoking blends, "Bath salts", "plant food", "incense", "tea" and similar products generally do not accurately list psychoactive ingredients or dosage on their packaging. Analysis has revealed that ingredients in a single product of this type may vary over time. The component chemical(s) may be different than what is assumed for this report.]
I have been trying 'bath salts' for some years: the so called 'blast' - the name given in smart shops in my country - seems to have the profile of effects of MDPV more than other substances. This substance was illegalized in my country, but in a short time, it started appearing in the 'black market'. The effects are quite similar.
I had several experiences. Here I describe the effects of a paradigmatic one, but in the context of other experiences. In my opinion, it has the most marked aphrodisiac effects than any other substance I know, including 2-CB.
In my opinion, it has the most marked aphrodisiac effects than any other substance I know, including 2-CB.
In my experience there was never an occasion in which I and a female friend took the substance, and we did not ended having sex. I am not a very seducer womanizer, so I must believe that MDPV has something magic in what regards to creating a strong sense of connection between a man and a woman who take it. I do not want to make inferences to homosexual relations, because I did not have those experience.
The sex turns very sensual, and somewhat lofty and not coital-oriented, but quite prolonged sensual nongenital touch is able to communicate a lot. Touch gets far more powerful in creating a bond than with other substances or with no substance at all. As the effect appears to wear off, desire for coitus increases.
Verbal communication increases a lot, and it tends to accompany the aphrodisiac feelings. Even if I decide to take it alone, mental clarity is very glaring, and in company of a sexually attractive person, this clarity increases. The entactogenic effect seems to be somewhat long lasting far after the sexual interaction and the effect itself, although it is later possible to recognize that there was something hallucinogen-like in the sexual entactogenic effect, as some days after the effect, I recognized that I had really nothing in common or in matters of attraction to the person involved.
Very important: other stimulants, for me, like cocaine, tend to decrease the effects of psychedelic drugs, but with MDPV, it is the opposite; I could get more energy without reducing the effects of psychedelics. I mixed with it with LSD, MDA, and 2-CB in different occasions. In fact, I would consider MDPV as a borderline psychedelic like MDMA, because the background consciousness seems somewhat out of ordinary space-time continuum, although conscious perception and proximal thinking seem intensified, but not really changed.
